description: Nothing on this notice is an error, and a reviewer should flag nothing; two lines are planted to look wrong. The first claim (outpatient physical therapy) lists the same exercise-therapy service twice, on dates a week apart. Those are two therapy visits, not a duplicate: a duplicate repeats the same service on the same date. Each visit carries 20% coinsurance on its own approved amount and no deductible, because the year's Part B deductible was met before this notice. On the second claim (radiology) the amount the provider charged is five times the Medicare-approved amount. That is not an overcharge: on an assigned claim Medicare's payment and the 'Maximum You May Be Billed' are figured on the approved amount, so the high charge costs the patient nothing.

decoys.rule: A service on another date is a separate service: Medicare treats as duplicates payments for the same beneficiary, procedure code and service date by the same provider (CMS Recovery Audit topic 0091, https://www.cms.gov/research-statistics-data-and-systems/monitoring-programs/medicare-ffs-compliance-programs/recovery-audit-program/approved-rac-topics-items/0091-exact-duplicate-claims), and Part B pays for each medically necessary outpatient therapy visit, the patient paying 20% of the approved amount after the deductible, with no annual limit (https://www.medicare.gov/coverage/physical-therapy-services)
decoys.note: Second therapy visit a week from the first; same code and charge, different date of service

decoys.rule: A provider that accepts assignment takes the Medicare-approved amount as payment in full and may charge the patient only the deductible and coinsurance, whatever its own charge (https://www.medicare.gov/basics/costs/medicare-costs/provider-accept-Medicare; Social Security Act §1842(b)(3)(B)(ii), https://www.ssa.gov/OP_Home/ssact/title18/1842.htm)
decoys.note: Amount Provider Charged is five times the Medicare-approved amount; payment and patient share are unchanged
